newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sets $50 mln minimum bid price for Mahr Tunel.
newsitem.headline: Peru sets $50 mln minimum bid price for Mahr Tunel.

text.p: Peruvian state miner Centromin said Thursday it had fixed a $50 million minimum bid price for the privatization of its Mahr Tunel SA subsidiary.
Centromin spokesman Enrique Olivares also told Reuters that the sale had been put back to July 18, and the successful buyer would be required to invest a minimum of $60 million over five years.
"The base price for 100 percent of the shares in Mahr Tunel has been fixed at $50 million," he said. "An investment of $60 million in five years will be demanded."

Centromin was due to formally take offers on June 16 and announce the winner June 20. "The new date for the presentation of proposals is July 14 and the opening of envelopes Friday, July 18," Olivares added.
He said this delay was because three of the 11 companies interested had requested more time to prepare their bids.

The seven foreign companies interested are Sweden's Boliden AB, Mexico's Industrias Penoles SA, Grupo Mexico SA and Minera Penoles del Peru, Switzerland's Glencore International, Australia's Savage Resources Ltd, and the United States' Sunshine Mining and Refining CO.
Local companies Minsur SA, Volcan, Morococha SA and Arcata Hoschild are also interested in bidding, according to Centromin.
Mahr Tunel SA controls the San Cristobal and Andaychagua mines, which lie close to each other in the central Peruvian highlands.
Last year, San Cristobal produced 680,000 dry tonnes of ore containing zinc, lead, copper and silver, while Andaychagua produced about 395,000 dry tonnes of ore with silver, lead and zinc.
